newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down on correction.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed down on Friday on a correction following Thursday's sharp gains, brokers said.
The B index inched down 0.270 points or 0.41 percent to 65.157 points, on volume of 17.8 million shares worth $8.5 million, down from $10.8 million on Thursday.
Brokers said institutional support helped the market reverse some of the morning's losses and the index is likely to hit the 68-point resistance level in the short term.
Property developer Lujiazui performanced worse on institutional selling, ending down $0.010 or 1.19 percent to $0.826 on volume of 1.7 million shares.

Tientsin Marine Shipping was the most active share and closed up on speculative buying ahead of the close despite falls for the most of the session, rising $0.002 or 0.39 percent to $0.512 on volume of 1.8 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index reversed early losss on speculative buying, but trading remaining slow on cautious market sentiment, brokers said.
"The index will try to test the 68-point level ahead of the Chinese lunar new year holiday, but heavy resistance is expected given the lack of good news from the Nanjing meeting," he added.
The securities authorities held a meeting in Nanjing this week to help prepare Chinese companies chosen for listings on overseas markets.

Of 43 B shares, 39 traded, with 20 down, six flat and 13 up. Hotel group Shanghai Jinjiang Tower was the biggest loser on expectations of unpromising results, slipping $0.018 or 6.04 percent to $0.280 on volume of 158,800 shares.
The A index rose 8.86 points or 0.89 percent to 995.50 points on volume of 344.3 million shares worth 3.2 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 18.34 points or 0.72 percent to 2571.89 points.
Shanghai Shenhua Industry was the star on rumours of a bonus offering, soaring 10 percent to its limit-up of 15.27 yuan on volume of 6.8 million shares.
